fullPassage: The most prevalent problem kids report is that they feel like they need to be accessible at all times. Because technology allows for it, they feel an obligation. It's easy for most of us to relate — you probably feel the same pressure in your own life! It is really challenging to deal with the fact that we're human and can't always respond instantly. For a teen or tween who's still learning the ins and outs of social interactions, it's even worse. Here's how this behavior plays out sometimes: Your child texts one of his friends, and the friend doesn't text back right away. Now it's easy for your child to think, "This person doesn't want to be my friend anymore!" So he texts again, and again, and again — "blowing up their phone." This can be stress-inducing and even read as aggressive. But you can see how easily this could happen.

det.tip: deal with: (과제/문제를) 처리하다 vs (어려운 상황/사람을) 대처하다. 본문의 deal with the fact = 사실에 대처하다

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어는?

"able to be reached or entered; easy to contact or communicate with"

det.korean: 도달하거나 들어갈 수 있는; 연락하거나 소통하기 쉬운 → accessible
det.analysis:
❌ ① prevalent — 만연한 (널리 퍼진 것이지 접근 가능이 아님)
❌ ② aggressive — 공격적인 (의미 무관)
❌ ③ challenging — 어려운 (접근 가능과 반대 뉘앙스)
✅ ④ accessible — 접근 가능한 ←정답
det.tip: accessible = 접근 가능한, 이용 가능한. be accessible at all times = 항상 연락 가능한 상태

questions.passage: It is really __________ (challenge) to deal with the fact that we're human and can't always respond instantly.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 항상 즉시 응답할 수 없다는 사실을 다루는 것은 정말 '어려운' 일이다 → 형용사 challenging
det.analysis: It is really __________ to deal with → it is + 형용사 보어 자리. challenge(동사/명사) → challenging(형용사)로 변환. It is challenging to ~ = ~하는 것은 어렵다.
det.tip: challenge(도전, 동사: 도전하다) → challenging(어려운, 형용사). It is challenging to V = V하는 것은 어렵다

questions.passage: For a teen or tween who's still __________ (learn) the ins and outs of social interactions, it's even worse.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 사회적 상호작용의 이모저모를 아직 '배우고 있는' 십대에게는 더 나쁘다 → 현재분사 learning
det.analysis: who's still __________ the ins and outs → who is still + 현재분사(진행형). learn(동사) → learning(현재분사)로 변환. be still learning = 아직 배우고 있다.
det.tip: learn(배우다) → learning(배우고 있는, 현재분사). who is still learning = 아직 배우고 있는

questions.passage: The most prevalent problem kids report is that they feel like they need to be accessible at all times. Because technology allows for it, they feel an obligation. It's easy for most of us to relate — you probably feel the same pressure in your own life! It is really challenging to deal with the fact that we're human and can't always respond instantly. For a teen or tween who's still learning __________ of social interactions, it's even worse. Here's how this behavior plays out sometimes: Your child texts one of his friends, and the friend doesn't text back right away. Now it's easy for your child to think, "This person doesn't want to be my friend anymore!" So he texts again, and again, and again — "blowing up their phone." This can be stress-inducing and even read as aggressive. But you can see how easily this could happen.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사회적 상호작용의 '이모저모'를 아직 배우고 있는 십대에게는 더 나쁘다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① the ups and downs — 기복, 부침 (social interactions의 세부 사항이 아닌 감정적 변화)
❌ ② the rights and wrongs — 옳고 그름 (도덕적 판단이지 세부 사항 학습이 아님)
✅ ③ the ins and outs — 이모저모, 세부 사항. learning the ins and outs = 세세한 것까지 배우다 ←정답
❌ ④ the pros and cons — 장단점 (social interactions의 장단점을 배운다는 것은 부자연)
det.tip: the ins and outs = 이모저모, 세부 사항. learn the ins and outs of = ~의 이모저모를 배우다

questions.passage: The most prevalent problem kids report is that they feel like they need to be accessible at all times. Because technology allows for it, they feel an obligation. It's easy for most of us to relate — you probably feel the same pressure in your own life! It is really challenging to deal with the fact that we're human and can't always respond instantly. For a teen or tween who's still learning the ins and outs of social interactions, it's even worse. Here's how this behavior plays out sometimes: Your child texts one of his friends, and the friend doesn't text back right away. Now it's easy for your child to think, "This person doesn't want to be my friend anymore!" So he texts again, and again, and again — "__________." This can be stress-inducing and even read as aggressive. But you can see how easily this could happen.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그래서 그는 계속해서 문자를 보내고 — 즉 '상대방의 폰을 폭주시킨다.'
det.analysis:
❌ ① hanging up the phone — 전화를 끊다 (반복 문자 맥락과 반대)
✅ ② blowing up their phone — 폰을 폭주시키다. 반복적으로 문자를 보내는 행위를 묘사 ←정답
❌ ③ picking up the phone — 전화를 받다 (문자를 보내는 행동이지 받는 것이 아님)
❌ ④ turning off their phone — 폰을 끄다 (반복 문자와 반대 행동)
det.tip: blow up one's phone = 폰에 문자/전화를 폭주시키다. 반복 문자로 상대를 압박하는 행위
